title: fix(ui): reveal clipped sidebar identity names
body:
Closes #151378 ## What Problem This Solves Long identity names in the sidebar are clipped without a way to reveal the hidden text. ## User Impact Overflowing account, agent, and workspace names have a short fade and scroll to the end and back on hover or keyboard focus. Tapping keeps the existing menu interaction. Short names remain static; reduced motion disables the animation and the full name remains accessible. ## Why This Change Was Made The three identity rows share the avatar/name/menu pattern. They now use the existing measured marquee owner with a 20px fade, 300ms initial delay, and 35px/s CSS loop. Only actual overflow is faded. The trailing fade disappears at the endpoint, Arabic names move in the appropriate direction, and hidden drawer names stop animating. ## Evidence Before: production build of merge-base `a225ce456f2aa32a8857893cb24770aa680429e2`. After captures: production build at `78c203e87bf6ec7aa2ab9848334ef951b17571e0`. Current head: `6a00cb16c75e7721c8f0bbf39bd1b564e69fb0ff`, rebased onto `90f47f2e7a0076308f387a33e1faec85a11408ac` with all three patches unchanged. Sidebar identity code and styles match the captured implementation; the only upstream edit within these production files removes unrelated chat-streaming CSS. Later test commits complete browser fixtures and align native-navigation expectations with short-name behavior. Both use identical synthetic fixtures, fonts, viewports, and capture settings. All images and the video contain synthetic names.

The 19-second recording shows the account and agent names revealing their endings and returning at normal speed. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ea7af51-cebc-411e-b3d5-c1baf5cc3018 - Regression proof: the long-name case fails on the merge-base because its fade is missing; all 9 new end-to-end cases pass on this branch. - 455 existing UI and browser tests pass, including shared marquee lifecycle, identity/agent menus, and native-navigation geometry. A focused rerun passes all 16 identity-name and native-navigation E2E cases; short names remain unfaded in LTR and RTL page chrome. - Production matrix: 25 cases covering short, long, very long, emoji, and Arabic names; light/dark; 1440px/390px; workspace, hover, keyboard focus, reduced motion, touch, and collapsed navigation. All pass, with 38 overflowing-name observations at 35px/s, zero sidebar layout shifts, and zero page errors. - Production build, UI typecheck, the affected UI test type graphs, TypeScript lint, style lint, and line/assertion ratchets pass. Core type graphs also passed in the broader validation run; the final corrections only affect UI test fixtures. Post-rebase validation at `6a00cb16c75e7721c8f0bbf39bd1b564e69fb0ff` passes all 20 focused tests, the complete changed-file checks, and the production build. Startup JavaScript is 359,960 bytes gzip against a 363,282-byte limit. [Hosted CI passes on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35320922224). ## Risk and coverage A source audit confirmed that session rows, catalog rows and headings, session group headings, the online heading, and person activity session links retain the shared marquee defaults and do not enable the new loop. Existing browser tests for shared marquee lifecycle pass. The looping option is limited to the account, agent, and workspace identity rows. Focus/menu behavior, displacement, RTL, reduced motion, and unchanged control geometry are covered by browser checks. The session header owns a rename action; agent chips are noninteractive labels and owner chips are avatar-only. Those surfaces are outside this change. No configuration, persistence, Gateway, or dependency changes are included. Touch proof uses Chromium touch emulation; physical mobile devices were not tested.
